about.title: A small team, a wide world
about.lead: GLOBAL DIGITAL UNIVERSE began as one person's twenty-year idea and grew into a digital business headquarters. Apps, writing and channels are gathered here under a single brand.

blocks.label: WHAT WE DO
blocks.title: From concept to operations
blocks.body: Product planning, brand design, web engineering, content production and channel operations are handled in-house. We ship directly and revise against real user response every week.

blocks.label: HOW WE BUILD
blocks.title: Free infrastructure, paid-grade craft
blocks.body: Every service starts on free infrastructure: zero server cost, domain attached in a later phase. Quality comes from design decisions, not from budget.

blocks.label: WHERE WE STAND
blocks.title: A brand that is not tied to one character
blocks.body: KOMI and MOMO are beloved characters, but they are not the whole brand. GLOBAL DIGITAL UNIVERSE is the vessel that lets new services keep being born.

principles: Build only what people actually use.
Design inside free limits, and check the limits first.
Keep the brand name and menus editable from the admin.
Never delete originals; keep every draft restorable.

abi.title: ABI — an AI assistant that remembers on your phone
abi.lead: ABI is a standalone Android AI assistant that keeps conversations and memory in the phone's own SQLite and reaches the cloud only when it needs to. It is in phase-one beta, distributed as an APK rather than through a store.
abi.whyTitle: A conversation stays where it happened — on the phone
abi.whyBody: ABI began with one idea: an assistant that lives inside the phone. Conversations, memory and tasks accumulate in the device's SQLite, so reopening the app restores the context exactly as it was. Only heavy inference is meant for the cloud, and the route is chosen in settings, not by default.
abi.architectureTitle: Stored locally first, cloud only when needed
abi.architectureLead: ABI is a hybrid by design: memory is collected on the device, and only heavy inference travels to the cloud. Phase one builds the skeleton of that structure — the store, the route-selection logic and the approval policy — and leaves the model connection to phase two.

layers.title: On-device memory — SQLite
layers.body: Conversations, the user's preferences, facts and instructions, task records and approval logs are written to the app's own SQLite. Reopening the app keeps the conversation, and every memory can be added, edited or deleted directly.

layers.title: Hybrid route — local · free cloud · automatic
layers.body: The route is chosen in settings: work the phone can finish stays local, heavier inference goes to a free cloud tier. The router that decides this already exists in phase one; the model connection itself is phase two.

layers.title: Approval and key storage — Android Keystore
layers.body: API keys are never hardcoded: they live in SecureStore (Android Keystore) and are masked on screen. Tool runs pass through an approval policy that records both approvals and refusals.

abi.phaseTitle: What phase one does, and what was left out on purpose
phaseIn: Four tabs: conversation, memory, tasks, settings
Input → SQLite → the conversation survives a restart
Add, edit and delete preferences, facts and instructions
Approval policy, approval and refusal records, run audit log
Route selection, key masking and data deletion
phaseOut: Local AI inference (an LLM runtime) — deferred to phase two.
Outbound API code — there is no HTTP client in the app at all.
Real tool execution (notifications, calendar, messages) — the tool registry is empty.
abi.phaseNote: Phase-one chat replies are guidance text marked 'PHASE 1 · TEST RESPONSE', not model output. What is being validated now is the structure of storage, memory and approval — not conversational quality.
installSteps: Clone the repository and install dependencies with npm install.
Check the setup with npm run typecheck, npm run config and npm run doctor.

Build a development APK with npx eas-cli login → npx eas-cli init → npm run build:apk:eas. With JDK 17 and the Android SDK installed, npm run prebuild:android followed by gradlew assembleDebug builds it locally.
Install the APK on the phone and connect it to the development build server with npm start. Expo Go alone will not run it.
abi.installNote: This is a test APK, not a store release. The build procedure is documented in the repository under docs/CI_ANDROID_APK.md and ci/android-debug-apk.yml.

games.title: The world of KOMI and MOMO
games.lead: We extend our character IP into games. Two are playable today; one more is in production.

kCulture.title: Korean texture, in the world's languages
kCulture.lead: Dancheong, minhwa and myeongri — Korean materials translated into forms a global audience can read. No Chinese characters, only the reader's own language.

pillars.title: KOMI — Character
pillars.body: A long-haired chihuahua who loves Korea introduces K-beauty, K-food, K-golf and K-places.

pillars.title: MANSE — Reading
pillars.body: K-Sajoo reads saju and compatibility from real astronomical calendars, in fifteen languages.

pillars.title: PATTERN — Motif
pillars.body: The colours and patterns of dancheong and minhwa return as stickers, backdrops and goods.

media.title: Eight channels
media.lead: One piece of content is rewritten for each channel's language and grammar. Korea runs on blog, cafe and Threads; the world on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and Xiaohongshu.
